criteria_text.A1: selected judge T0 parse rate >= 0.95 on every pool
criteria_text.A2: T3 sign agreement >= 0.80 over reward x pool x rule cells whose human-gain 95% bootstrap interval excludes zero
criteria_text.A3: T3 Spearman correlation between judge gain and human gain across all cells >= 0.60
criteria_text.A4: Among cells where human gain is significantly negative (reward selection hurts humans), the judge gain is negative in >= 0.80 of them; if there are fewer than 5 such cells, A4 is reported as underpowered rather than passed
criteria_text.decision: Accept the judge as the development proxy for generative-RL evaluation only if A1-A3 pass and A4 is not failed. Otherwise report failure and do not use the judge for headline claims.

analysis.inconclusive_rule: If any primary comparison is undefined because a pressure target is unreachable or an analysis stratum is absent, report the criterion as inconclusive; do not impute, replace the endpoint, or tune the grid.

analysis.success_criterion: The primary selector has lower mean held-out decision regret than every fixed-pressure baseline and best-of-N, and its interval excludes zero for the contrast with the strongest non-oracle baseline.
analysis.uncertainty: hierarchical bootstrap resampling reward-training seed and evaluation document; external controls reported separately

outcomes.human_quality: candidate-level released human score aggregated by its official protocol; larger-is-better direction fixed in the dataset manifest
outcomes.primary: held-out decision regret: oracle held-out human quality minus human quality at the selector's pressure, averaged over learned reward checkpoints
outcomes.reporting: Show complete pressure curves and every reward checkpoint, including failed, degenerate, and unreachable runs.
secondary: selected raw and normalized KL pressure

policy.reward_standardization: mean zero and unit variance on the unlabeled optimization pool
policy.scorer: one shared linear vector; no system identity and no bias

pressure.checkpoint_rule: first recorded checkpoint reaching each target; preserve the final checkpoint and mark every unreached target unavailable
pressure.interpretation: zero is uniform and one is maximum concentration
pressure.measure: mean KL(pi || uniform) divided by log(number of available actions), computed on the unlabeled optimization pool
pressure.unreachable_rule: A selector may choose only a target reached by every reward checkpoint being compared in its analysis stratum. No outcome is imputed.

primary_selector.calibration_score: within-segment candidate human scores standardized by the segment standard deviation, then expected under each frozen policy checkpoint and averaged equally over calibration documents
primary_selector.decision_artifact_rule: Write and hash every per-reward pressure decision before evaluation labels are opened.
primary_selector.decision_rule: Among jointly reachable pressure targets, choose the target with the largest mean calibration human-quality change from uniform; ties within exact floating-point equality choose the smaller pressure. The zero-pressure action is always available.
primary_selector.human_feedback: candidate human scores for the frozen calibration segment from each calibration document and train-system candidates only
primary_selector.name: bounded human-calibration pressure argmax

safe_pressure_protocol.research_question: Can a bounded calibration audit choose a reward-optimization pressure that reduces held-out human-quality decision regret relative to fixed pressure, best-of-N, always-optimize, and always-keep baselines?

reward_models.all_runs_rule: Retain and report every scheduled reward run.
reward_models.external_controls: Freeze exact public checkpoint revisions in the future manifest; report them separately because checkpoints are not reward-training replicates.
reward_models.training_control: Architecture, initialization distribution, optimizer, budget, and score calibration are identical across learned conditions.

secondary_selectors.best_of_n: exact expected calibration human change for uniformly sampled candidate subsets; choose its best prespecified N or keep uniform
secondary_selectors.first_order_sign: completed sign rule applied without modification as a historical baseline
secondary_selectors.pessimistic_calibration: choose the pressure with the largest document-bootstrap lower confidence bound on calibration human change; choose zero unless that bound is positive

safe_pressure_protocol_amendment_1.amendment: Replace the label-free initial_concentration_rate diagnostic with normalized KL after one frozen exact-gradient update.
safe_pressure_protocol_amendment_1.justification: KL from the uniform policy has zero first derivative at the uniform policy, so the originally named first-order KL change is identically zero. The one-update quantity is the first nonzero, operational concentration diagnostic and uses no human outcome.
safe_pressure_protocol_amendment_1.scope: Label-free secondary mechanism diagnostic only; the primary selector, pressure grid, baselines, endpoint, and success criterion are unchanged.

safe_pressure_protocol_amendment_2.amendment: Treat a best-of-N subset size larger than the frozen train-system action count as structurally unavailable and select only among valid prespecified sizes.
safe_pressure_protocol_amendment_2.justification: The frozen balanced system split has seven train-system actions, so the prespecified N=8 baseline cannot be defined. N=2 and N=4 remain unchanged. No replacement N is introduced.
safe_pressure_protocol_amendment_2.scope: Best-of-N baseline feasibility only; the primary selector, pressure grid, endpoint, and success criterion are unchanged.

safe_pressure_protocol_amendment_3.amendment: Define best-of-N as a direct candidate-selection baseline. Calibration chooses among uniform selection and each structurally valid frozen N; evaluation applies the chosen N to the held-out-system candidate pool.
safe_pressure_protocol_amendment_3.justification: The original protocol named best-of-N but did not define which policy-pressure checkpoint an optimize decision would receive. Direct best-of-N is the standard procedure and avoids introducing an outcome-dependent pressure target.
safe_pressure_protocol_amendment_3.scope: Clarifies the prespecified best-of-N baseline only; the primary pressure selector, endpoint, pressure grid, and success criterion are unchanged.

tokenization_paper.scope: same-string estimator validation and NLLB length-tilt feasibility; no RL training effect

notes: Joint probability is p_theta(string) times q_phi(path|string).
Ordinary response-mean REINFORCE is invariant to q_phi for string-only reward.
Global token mean uses each sampled batch's total token count, so its expected sample weighting depends on q_phi.
Position weighting is an explicit alternative estimator and must not be confused with the joint behavior score.
synthetic.scope: exact finite synthetic policy; not an MT result
